svg.text: 237 · The three-quarter exponent for honeycomb self-avoiding walk
Exact enumeration of every self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice up to n = 40 steps (190,380,602,052 walks at n = 40).
c_n matches OEIS A001668 term by term. Finite data illustrate the exponent; they do not prove it.
even and odd n alternate, both falling toward μ
D. One 1000-step walk on the honeycomb
start (rust) to end (teal); diameter 179.1 edge lengths, n^(3/4) = 177.8
sample from a pivot Markov chain, seed 237, 9383 of 40000 pivots accepted;
The theorem (OpenAI, Sept 2026) is about diameter, local mass and covering numbers of a uniform n-step walk: diameter n^(3/4+o(1)),
mass exponent 4/3, and R_g = n^(3/4+o(1)). It explicitly does not give a lower bound on the end-to-end distance |w_n|.
Enumerator: C, depth-first with the six-fold symmetry of the first two steps; all sums are exact integers.
